Abstract Early detection of Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is crucial for preventing vision impairment. In this paper, we propose a vision transformer (ViT) architecture coupled with Grad-CAM++ feature visualization to deliver interpretable, high-accuracy lesion localization on high-resolution fundus images.
Key Contributions Achieved 96.4% diagnostic sensitivity across standard benchmark datasets. Developed an open-source PyTorch interpretation package for clinical heatmaps. Validated model explanations with certified ophthalmologists. Citation @article{hossain2025explainable, title={Explainable Deep Learning for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy}, author={Hossain, Muhammad Rabiul and et al.}, journal={IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging}, year={2025}, publisher={IEEE} } 🔗 Links: DOI: 10.1109/TMI.2025.321456 | GitHub Repository
summary: Proposed a novel Grad-CAM++ integrated vision transformer framework that highlights clinical lesion regions with 96.4% diagnostic accuracy.
title: Explainable Deep Learning for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy

content:
Introduction Vision Transformers (ViT) have revolutionized computer vision by replacing traditional convolutional layers with multi-head self-attention mechanisms. In this post, we unpack how patches are extracted and processed.
Patch Tokenization Given an image $X \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}$, we flatten it into 2D patches $X_p \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times (P^2 \cdot C)}$, where $(P, P)$ is the resolution of each image patch.
$$N = \frac{HW}{P^2}$$
Self-Attention Calculation The Query ($Q$), Key ($K$), and Value ($V$) projections are computed as:
$$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V$$
This allows the model to compute global pairwise patch dependencies across the entire image.
summary: A comprehensive deep dive into self-attention, patch embeddings, and multi-head attention visual explanations for computer vision.
title: Understanding Attention Mechanisms in Vision Transformers

content: Overview This research paper addresses signal spoofing threats in automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast (ADS-B) flight tracking. We introduce a hybrid XAI model that detects injection anomalies and provides interpretable feature risk scores for air traffic management.
summary: Hybrid machine learning and Explainable AI (XAI) framework for detecting spoofed ADS-B signal injection attacks in aviation telemetry.
title: Hybrid Explainable Models for Aviation Security: Detecting ADS-B Injection Attacks with XAI Techniques
